title: Probing the network
summary: curl, ss, dig, ping and traceroute: find out which layer is broken.

steps.title: curl: talk HTTP from the shell
body: ```text
curl https://api.example.com/health            # GET, body to stdout
curl -i https://api.example.com/health         # include response headers
curl -v https://api.example.com/health         # verbose: DNS, TCP, TLS, request and response headers
curl -fsS -o out.json https://...              # -f fail on HTTP errors (exit 22), -s silent, -S still show errors, -o save
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"qty":2}' https://api.example.com/orders
curl -L http://example.com                     # follow redirects
curl -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://...   # just status and timing
wget https://example.com/file.tar.gz           # simple downloads (resumes with -c)
In scripts and health checks always use `-f`: without it curl exits 0 even on a 500.

steps.prompt: Send JSON to the API and make the script fail on any HTTP error status.
steps.explain: `-f` turns 4xx/5xx into a non-zero exit, `-H` adds a header, `-d` sends a body.

steps.title: ss: who is listening?
body: `ss` (the modern `netstat`) shows sockets.
```text
$ sudo ss -tlnp
State   Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port  Peer Address:Port Process
`-t` TCP, `-u` UDP, `-l` listening only, `-n` numbers not names, `-p` show the process (needs sudo for others' processes).
**`127.0.0.1:5000` only accepts connections from the same machine.** `0.0.0.0` (or `*`, or `[::]`) means every interface. Half of "it works on the server but not from my laptop" tickets are this.

steps.prompt: From your laptop, `curl http://10.0.0.5:5000` says *Connection refused*. On the server, `curl localhost:5000` works and `ss -tlnp` shows `127.0.0.1:5000 dotnet`. What's wrong?
options: The app listens only on loopback; bind it to 0.0.0.0 (e.g. `ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://0.0.0.0:5000`) or put a reverse proxy in front
steps.explain: Refused (not a timeout) means the host answered but nothing listens on that address:port. A timeout would point to a firewall.

steps.title: dig, ping, traceroute
body: Work **up** the layers: is the name resolving, is the host reachable, is the port open, does the app answer?
```text
dig api.example.com +short            # name -> IP   (nslookup api.example.com is the older tool)
dig MX example.com                    # other record types
dig @8.8.8.8 api.example.com          # ask a specific resolver
ping -c 4 10.0.0.5                    # ICMP reachability and round-trip time
traceroute 10.0.0.5                   # each router hop on the way (tracepath / mtr are alternatives)
nc -zv 10.0.0.5 5432                  # is this TCP port open?
curl -v https://api.example.com       # does the app answer?
Note: many cloud networks block ICMP, so **a failed ping doesn't prove the host is down**.

steps.prompt: Arrange the checks for "the API is unreachable" from the lowest layer up.
steps.explain: Name resolution, then reachability, then the port, then the application. Each step narrows which team you need to call.

steps.prompt: Which symptom points to which cause?
items: HTTP 503 from the app's health check

steps.prompt: What does this print, assuming the server answers 404 in 0.12 s?
steps.explain: Without `-f`, curl treats any HTTP response as success, so the exit code is 0. With `-f` the exit code would be 22.
